chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Husayn al-Ahmasi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Paradise will say, 'O Lord, You filled the Fire just as You promised it, so fill me [as well] just as You promised me!' So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, will create a creation and make them enter Paradise.
Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Blessed are they, for they [shall] neither [have] witnessed the sorrows of the world nor its worries.'
ai.seo_question: What does Paradise say to God regarding the filling of Hellfire and Paradise?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the eschatological abundance of Paradise, where God creates a new creation to fill Jannah after Hell is full, emphasizing the concept of *jadid al-khalq* (new creation). It underscores the Shia spiritual ideal of detachment from worldly anxieties, linking the physical reality of Paradise with the spiritual state of those who transcended the *ghumum* (sorrows) of dunya. This reflects the theological view that Paradise is not merely a static reward but a dynamic realm of continuous divine generosity.
